# Reimplementation of the described analysis:
# Logistic regression predicting binary `response` from age, dose, biomarker.
# - scikit-learn LogisticRegression with default settings, max_iter=1000
# - train_test_split holding out 25% at random with random_state=42
# - metric: classification accuracy on the held-out rows
#
# Standard choices made where the methods are silent:
# - test_size=0.25 corresponds to "held out 25% of the rows"
# - train_test_split's default shuffle=True is used (rows are held out at random)
# - the split seed (42) fully determines the result; LogisticRegression with the
#   default lbfgs solver is deterministic, so no additional seeding is needed.

import json

import pandas as pd
from sklearn.linear_model import LogisticRegression
from sklearn.metrics import accuracy_score
from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split

DATA_PATH = "/work/repo/data/trials.csv"
OUT_PATH = "reimplementation_result.json"

# Load data
df = pd.read_csv(DATA_PATH)

FEATURES = ["age", "dose", "biomarker"]
TARGET = "response"

X = df[FEATURES]
y = df[TARGET]

# Hold out 25% of rows at random for testing, seed 42
X_train, X_test, y_train, y_test = train_test_split(
    X, y, test_size=0.25, random_state=42
)

# Logistic regression, scikit-learn defaults, up to 1000 iterations
model = LogisticRegression(max_iter=1000)
model.fit(X_train, y_train)

# Classification accuracy on the held-out rows
y_pred = model.predict(X_test)
accuracy = accuracy_score(y_test, y_pred)

json.dump({"value": float(accuracy)}, open(OUT_PATH, "w"))
